problem: Model-free RL fine-tuning of a pre-trained navigation policy needs a pre-trained critic; otherwise the actor is quickly overwritten by an untrained critic, causing instability and many human interventions. Residual RL composes in action space and struggles with complex base policies, while pure model-based learning is limited by model errors and dataset coverage.
motivation: Real-world social navigation needs robots to self-improve in the deployment environment (small or transparent obstacles, uneven floors, pedestrian interaction) without dangerous failures or heavy human supervision. Model-based objectives used offline (e.g. SACSoN) can also serve as a free critic initialization, so online RL can start from model-based behavior and then improve.
key_idea: Decompose the critic as Q(s,τ) = J_model(s,τ) + Q̄(s,a), where J is the offline differentiable model-based objective and Q̄ is a small residual critic learned online with TD3, so the actor is fine-tuned in objective space starting from the pre-trained behavior.
insight: Because Q̄ is initialized near zero, the initial Q equals the model-based objective and the policy is not disrupted. Online experience then adds the terms the model cannot capture (small/transparent obstacles, bumpy floors, long-horizon returns). Baselines confirm this: Residual RL (action-space composition) with the SACSoN base policy (Residual RL†) degrades (SPL 0.598, Int 9.4) versus Ours (SPL 0.932, Int 0.6) in Env 1; the authors hypothesize the residual policy must copy the complex base policy. Intervention curves show SELFI does not degrade over the first laps, unlike baselines. Adding 50 h of in-domain offline RL data reduces interventions further.
method: Hybrid critic: Q(s,τ)=J(s,τ)+Q̄(s,a), with J the SACSoN model-based trajectory objective (pose, geometry, pedestrian, regularization rewards) and Q̄ a learned residual capturing unmodeled rewards and the long-horizon tail; Q̄ initialized with small weights.

Actor fine-tuning: TD3 variant; the actor outputs an 8-step action sequence τ and is updated (1 actor update per 2 critic updates) by backpropagating through Q(s,τ) with a frozen pre-trained encoder. Assumes J(s,τ)≈γJ(s',τ') in the TD target.

Offline pre-training: encoder and actor trained on the 80-hour HuRoN dataset (>4000 human-robot interactions) by maximizing the differentiable SACSoN objective; inputs are 6 omnidirectional frames plus a goal image, with the previous action concatenated to handle actuator delay.
Online reward: r = v·ĝ + C_s + C_d, using bumper collision (0.3), IMU bumpiness (0.3), and intimate-distance violation (0.1) if d_h<0.5+r_r from YOLO segmentation and monocular depth; γ=0.97.

Asynchronous training system: a workstation trains with 50/50 online/offline batches (size 76, Adam 1e-4) and sends actor weights to the robot every 50 steps (~1 min); the robot adds Gaussian exploration noise, runs at 3 Hz on a Jetson Orin, and trains for up to 2 h or 15 laps (~6000 steps).

Localization and topological navigation: topological graph of goal images with poses from visual odometry plus AR markers to provide subgoal images and the goal-progress reward; the objective weight on Q̄ is gradually increased.

setting.backbone: Conv encoder (8 conv layers, 512-d) + MLP actor + 5-layer MLP residual critic; pre-trained with SACSoN, fine-tuned online with TD3 (trained from scratch, not pretrained foundation models)
setting.training_data: Offline: 80-hour HuRoN dataset (SACSoN). Online: up to 2 h / 15 laps of real-robot experience per environment. Variant: an additional 50 h of offline in-domain data from Environment 1 (Ours + prior data).
setting.observation: Omnidirectional RGB (Ricoh Theta S), 2 s history of 6 frames plus goal image; the reward uses a T265 tracking camera, AR markers, IMU and bumper
setting.action_space: Sequence of 8 future low-level velocity commands (v, ω) for a two-wheel-drive robot; the first action is executed at 3 Hz
setting.privileged: none at test time for the policy; training-time reward uses AR-marker/visual-odometry localization, bumper/IMU sensors and pedestrian detection. The sampling-based baseline uses GT goal pose.

numbers.eval_set_note: 5 laps in each of three real environments, organized setting with unseen small obstacles, mean over runs

results: On real-world social navigation, SELFI reaches SPL 0.918 and STL 0.739 versus 0.838/0.596 for the strongest baseline (SACSoN with fine-tuning), and cuts IDV (7.978 vs 18.018 s) and near-collision time by more than 50%. Interventions during online training drop to nearly zero by 15 laps, while baselines first worsen. Pre-training on 50 h of in-domain data further improves it (IDV 6.61, Int 0.2).
limitations: The balance between the model-based objective and the learned Q̄ cannot be predicted in advance and needs trial and error on the real robot (weight gradually increased).
Socialness reward covers only intimate-distance violations; localization relies on AR markers and a looped route, and the evaluation covers only one building and small runs (5 laps, 12 users).
